subject: Privacy SSQ: PII scoping & cross-border flow diagram request
messages:
From: Alice Johnson <alice.johnson@mediahealth.com>
To: Ava Chen <ava_chen@redwood.com>
Cc: security@mediahealth.com
Date: Tue, 18 Nov 2025 09:12:00 -0800
Subject: SSQ: PII mapping + cross-border flow diagram

Hi Ava,

Thanks for taking this on. Our compliance team is running a focused review ahead of an upcoming contract signature. Attached is MediaHealth's security and privacy questionnaire (redacted). The key asks we need answered by next week:

- A clear data flow diagram showing where PII enters, how it is processed, storage locations (cloud regions), and which subprocessors see identifiable tokens.
- A mapping of PII fields (PHI/PII) to Redwood product surfaces and retention policies; we need column-level examples.
- KMS / key custody details and whether keys are customer-managed or Redwood-managed for Private deployments.
- List of subprocessors with roles and any cross-border transfer rely points.

Can you provide a single PDF with the diagram, plus an XLSX mapping, and a short KMS attestation (.txt) we can attach to the SSQ? MediaHealth prefers receiving materials via a shared Drive link or DocuSign envelope.

Appreciate your help — we have a tentative board review on 11/27, so a response by COB 11/24 would be ideal.

Best,
Alice
Alice Johnson
Security & Privacy Lead, MediaHealth
From: Ava Chen <ava_chen@redwood.com>
To: Alice Johnson <alice.johnson@mediahealth.com>
Date: Tue, 18 Nov 2025 10:05:00 -08:00
Subject: Re: SSQ: PII mapping + cross-border flow diagram

Alice —

Thanks for the note and the SSQ. I'm looping in Marissa on privacy intake and Jonas on architecture so we can produce the diagram and the mapping in one deliverable. We'll aim for COB 11/24; if we hit blockers we'll let you know by 11/21.

Quick clarifying Qs:
- Do you need an infrastructure-level diagram (VM / cluster / region IDs) or a logical service flow (Ingress -> Inference -> Storage -> Export)?
- For KMS: is an outline of key custody + export controls sufficient, or do you require signed attestation on company letterhead?

Ava
Ava Chen
Director, Solutions Engineering | Redwood Inference
From: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>
To: Ava Chen <ava_chen@redwood.com>, Jonas Weber <jonas_weber@redwood.com>
Date: Wed, 19 Nov 2025 08:31:00 -08:00
Subject: Re: SSQ: PII mapping + cross-border flow diagram

Ava / Jonas —

Thanks for the heads up. Proposed split of work: I will own the PII classification matrix (column mapping, retention policy, sample pseudonymization rules) and produce the XLSX. Jonas — can you take the data flow diagram and annotate which subprocessors touch tokenized data vs plaintext? Please flag any cross-border hops (EU -> US etc) and the region controls we can cite.

On the KMS attestation: I'll draft a short statement describing customer-managed key options (Private) vs Redwood-managed keys (Hosted/Dedicated), and include where HSM/KMS proofs live. We may need Legal to review the attestation language; I'll send a draft later today.

Also: I'll include a simple slide describing acceptable redaction/pseudonymization patterns we recommend so MediaHealth has remediation steps.

Marissa
Principal Privacy Engineer | Redwood Inference
From: Jonas Weber <jonas_weber@redwood.com>
To: Alice Johnson <alice.johnson@mediahealth.com>, Ava Chen <ava_chen@redwood.com>, Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>
Date: Mon, 24 Nov 2025 11:48:00 -08:00
Subject: Re: SSQ: PII mapping + cross-border flow diagram

Alice —

Attached are the files you requested (Drive link below). Summary of what's included:

1) redwood_dataflow_v2.pdf — Logical and operational dataflow for request/response, inference cache boundaries, persistent storage, and outbound export paths. Diagram flags three subprocessors: S3-compatible storage (US region), telemetry cluster (EU region), and logging/archival vendor (US with EU mirror). Where data is tokenized in-flight is highlighted in orange.

2) pii-classification-matrix.xlsx — Column-level PII categories (PII / Sensitive / PHI), default retention windows, recommended redaction/pseudonymization technique per column, and sample query examples to avoid exporting full identifiers.

3) kms-attestation.txt — Short statement: for Private customers keys are customer-managed (bring-your-own-key supported via KMS integrations); for Dedicated/Hosted Redwood can manage keys but HSM-backed controls are used and key access is role-restricted. Legal-approved wording is attached.

Drive: https://drive.google.com/drive/folders/1a2b3c-redwood-mediahealth-ssq
DocuSign (if needed): https://app.docusign.com/rooms/ABCDEFG12345

If you'd like, we can schedule a 30-minute walkthrough on Wed 11/26 to go through the diagram and mapping.

— Jonas
Staff Applied Architect | Redwood Inference
(Attachment stubs: redwood_dataflow_v2.pdf, pii-classification-matrix.xlsx, kms-attestation.txt)
From: Alice Johnson <alice.johnson@mediahealth.com>
To: Jonas Weber <jonas_weber@redwood.com>, Ava Chen <ava_chen@redwood.com>, Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>
Date: Tue, 25 Nov 2025 15:03:00 -08:00
Subject: Re: SSQ: PII mapping + cross-border flow diagram

Jonas / Ava / Marissa —

This is perfect, thank you. I reviewed the PDF and the XLSX; the column examples are exactly what our reviewers wanted. The KMS attestation language is acceptable for the board packet. We'll share the SSQ with the compliance committee on Thursday and I expect one minor follow-up on the logging vendor mirror timing — I'll loop back if they ask.

Appreciate the quick turnaround and clear artifacts. A 30-min walkthrough on 11/26 at 10:00 PT would be helpful; please confirm.

Thanks,
Alice
